nearby.label: The Sun's neighbours (within 20 parsecs)
nearby.why: Our closest stellar neighbours: the best places to look for planets and to study faint, small stars.

white_dwarf_candidate.label: White dwarf candidates
white_dwarf_candidate.why: Earth-sized embers of dead stars, far fainter than normal stars of the same colour. This is what our Sun will become.

luminous_giant.label: Luminous giants
luminous_giant.rule: absolute magnitude M_G < −2 (no dust correction, so they are at least this bright)
luminous_giant.why: Swollen stars near the end of their lives, thousands of times brighter than the Sun; some may explode as supernovae.

fast_mover.label: Fast movers across the sky
fast_mover.why: Stars that visibly shift position within a human lifetime, usually because they are close or very fast.

hypervelocity_candidate.label: Hypervelocity candidates
hypervelocity_candidate.rule: speed relative to the Sun > 600 km/s (3D when a radial velocity exists, else across-sky only)
hypervelocity_candidate.why: Stars moving fast enough that they may escape the Milky Way, possibly flung out by the central black hole. Most turn out to be measurement problems: these need checking.

strong_wobble.label: Strong wobblers (RUWE > 10)
strong_wobble.why: Gaia's single-star model fails badly: often a hidden companion star, sometimes crowding or an instrument effect.

very_red.label: Very red stars
very_red.why: Extremely cool stars, or stars behind thick dust, or stars wrapped in their own dust.
